newsitem.title: USA: Madison Avenue warned about Puerto Rico parade.
newsitem.headline: Madison Avenue warned about Puerto Rico parade.

text.p: A business group on Madison Avenue urged members to close during the Puerto Rico Day parade scheduled for Sunday, sparking criticism Thursday from New York's mayor and Hispanic leaders.

The parade is a showcase for New York's 900,000 residents of Puerto Rican ancestry and draws huge festive crowds. It runs down Fifth Avenue, a block from Madison Avenue's exclusive boutiques and shops.

The Madison Avenue Business Improvement District group distributed leaflets to storekeepers reading: "We would advise that your establishment remain shut this Sunday...(and) the removal of expensive merchandise from your windows."
The flyers also referred to the parade date as a "difficult day."
Repubican Mayor Rudy Giuliani, who will be marching in the parade, said the group's remarks were "really quite ignorant."
Giuliani also said the city expected to generate $43 million in sales as a result of the parade and stores along Madison Avenue could take in as much as $3 million.
City officials expect between 2.5 million and 3 million spectators at Sunday's parade.
"This isn't the spirit of New York," said Bronx Borough President Freddie Ferrer, himself of Puerto Rican ancestry. He called the flyers "the work of small minds" and "a hysterical overreaction."
A spokeswoman for the business association said the leaflet arose from concerns about the beating death of a young man near Madison Avenue during St. Patrick's Day parade in March.
